conventions: A reflexive or reciprocal pronoun the ASV writes for a verb whose Hebrew has no object morpheme is kept in the verb's unit under rule 44's reflexive clause rather than marked added: 85.3 Hiphil הֱשִׁיבוֹתָ → 'turned thyself' (italic thyself), 85.10 Qal נָשָׁקוּ → 'have kissed each other' and Niphal נִפְגָּשׁוּ → 'are met together'. The competing reading (a supplied object, added) is named in each note; the chapter takes the reflexive reading throughout.

The one interrogative הַ opening the verse takes both 'Wilt's: the second colon תִּמְשֹׁךְ אַפְּךָ is asyndetic with no particle of its own, and the ASV rewrites the auxiliary at its head under the first particle's scope (rule 25's distributed interrogative, applied where no waw stands in the second colon). Giving the second Wilt to the verb under rule 17 was the competing reading.
report: Checked all 17 cross-verse candidate groups. Every difference is licensed by the ASV's own rendering: suffix possessive vs object (הוּא), rectum-of vs bare noun (עַם, אַף, יֵשַׁע), לְ as for/to/that/unrepresented per its own English, מִן out of vs from, waw and/And/That/But/unrepresented. No construction is analysed two ways.

שׁוּב five shapes are five constructions, each placed by its rule: 85.1 brought back and 85.8 turn again keep the particle with the verb (rule 44's own שׁוּב example); 85.3 Hiphil keeps the italic thyself under rule 44's reflexive clause; 85.4 bare imperative Turn; 85.6 auxiliary תָּשׁוּב before תְּחַיֵּנוּ takes again as its own unit under rule 56. Not a split.

The single added unit (85.13 'to walk in') is the only supplied English in the chapter answering to no morpheme; no other verse folds comparable material into a neighbour, so the added-blind table hides no split.

BSB disagreements (85.5 וָ + דֹר distributive repetition rendered once; 85.7, 85.9, 85.13 prepositions left wordless by the ASV's recasting; 85.8 article on אֵל with no the) are all documented convention differences under rules 22, 40 and 29. None is an error.

Head of 85.0 'Chief Musician' on Musician is a display choice already noted with its competing reading; a cross-chapter check of לַמְנַצֵּחַ heads would be a corpus-wide matter and does not change any edge here.
No promotions: the chapter applies existing rules and teaches nothing that generalises.
